slots.title: Bessent answers Warren on 10-year yield
slots.body:
The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield sits at 5.2% in the Oct. 8 treasury snapshot.

The gap between 2-year and 10-year yields is 0.47 percentage points on that same date.

Fox Business reports Scott Bessent responded to Elizabeth Warren’s letter asking for information on the rise in the 10-year Treasury yield.

Warren’s letter and Bessent’s reply put Washington’s attention on bond yields at a time when stocks finished higher on Oct. 10.

- $^GSPC +0.6% to 7,811.54
- $^VIX -3.7% to 14.84

slots.title: Supreme Court hears 401(k) private-fund case
slots.body:
CNBC reports the Supreme Court heard a major 401(k) case this week.

A former Intel employee argued plan fiduciaries breached their duty by investing in hedge funds and private equity, pointing in part to underperformance.

Lower courts had already rejected the claims, ruling underperformance alone is not enough without showing a meaningful benchmark for courts to judge performance.

The case sits at the intersection of retirement policy and how large employers allocate default savings — separate from where the S&P 500 closed Oct. 10.

- $^GSPC +0.6% to 7,811.54
- $^DJI +0.8% to 51,654.95

Do you track Supreme Court cases that could change how workplace retirement plans are run?

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 11, 2026
slots.body:
The Dow led the major U.S. indexes, closing at 51,654.95 (+0.8%, +423.31 points).
The S&P 500 finished at 7,811.54 (+0.6%) and the Nasdaq Composite at 27,366.17 (+0.6%).
The Russell 2000 rose to 2,806.98 (+0.5%).

The CBOE Volatility Index fell to 14.84, down 0.57 points (-3.7%), with an intraday range of 14.77 to 15.34 in the injected data.

Payment networks stood out among megacaps: Visa closed at 385.45 (+2.8%) with a session high of 386.84, and Mastercard at 589.14 (+2.7%).

Health-care heavyweights also closed higher: UnitedHealth at 379.30 (+2.3%), Johnson & Johnson at 261.44 (+1.9%), and AbbVie at 276.47 (+1.5%), with AbbVie’s session high at 277.60 matching its 52-week high in the quote file.

Tesla finished at 382.70 (+2.1%) on volume of 38,834,397 shares.
Alphabet Class A closed at 351.66 (+1.0%) and Class C at 347.86 (+0.9%).

Apple bucked the broader index tone, closing at 336.64 (-1.1%) after trading between 330.70 and 338.60.
Home Depot fell to 290.74 (-1.6%) and PepsiCo to 125.97 (-1.8%).

Telecom saw large percentage declines in the active-volume list: AT&T at 22.18 (-9.8%) and Verizon at 41.65 (-8.7%), both on the session’s most-active screen in the injected data.

Financials mixed with the tape: JPMorgan Chase at 332.99 (+0.5%) and Bank of America at 54.32 (+1.3%).
Meta Platforms closed at 718.67 (-0.3%).

Gold futures (GCUSD) settled at 4,216.30, up 59.30 (+1.4%).
Brent crude (BZUSD) was at 104.72 (+0.4%); the United States Oil Fund (USO) closed at 148.20 (+0.4%).

The Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund (UUP) ticked to 29.02 (+0.1%).
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was at 82,733.16 (-0.2%) in the cross-asset block.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-10-09) showed the 10-year at 5.2% and the 2s10s spread at 0.44 percentage points.
No sector ETF performance array was included in this payload, and the earnings calendar block was empty.
